name: Walking pad
lead: A walking pad is a slim, low-speed folding treadmill without handrails, designed to slide under a desk or sofa. Speeds usually top out at about 6 km/h.
It is used to add steady walking to desk days, increasing daily steps without leaving the home. For appearance, the appeal is more daily energy expenditure and less sitting.

paras: Walking at a slow pace increases energy expenditure above sitting, roughly 100 kcal per hour more in a pooled analysis of treadmill-desk lab studies, and reduces sitting time. Reviews of treadmill desks show small improvements in sitting time and some metabolic markers. I did not find trials of walking pads specifically, so the closest research on treadmill desks is used.

Typing accuracy and mouse precision can suffer while walking, and productivity effects are mixed. Cheap units may overheat, have overstated weight limits and be loud. The claim of thousands of extra fat-burning steps is plausible, but the fat loss depends on diet and total activity; slow walking is a modest calorie burn.

studies.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the effect of treadmill desks on energy expenditure, sitting time and cardiometabolic health in adults
